trickyParts: A batch is the call's own update and the run queued after it, decided under the room's state lock before the store call and only shrunk after the document lock (a member another batch stored is dropped); every committing transaction marks what it stored before it releases the locks, and an update stored alone is a batch of one with the same protocol, so no update is stored twice (TestALoneUpdateAndABatchHoldingItStoreItOnce, three orders).

The gate reads the room cursor once the document's lock is held (appendGate.throughUnderLock): read before the lock, a settlement or live write holding it meanwhile moves the cursor and the gate would refuse wrongly.

The batched owed-settlement row folds last_actor and main's last_person exactly as one-at-a-time appends leave them (owedUpdates; TestABatchLeavesThePendingAuthorRowsOneAtATimeAppendsLeave with person/session/two-peer cases).

Own writes end in the head tracker through store.AfterCommit before the committing call returns, so a process reads its own writes; a transaction the pool did not open marks the document untrusted until its next head notification.

Shutdown: browser appends no longer strand a shared connection on a dead database, which exposed a pre-existing hang: pool.Close waited forever on a connection taken after the drain saw the pools idle. closePool now follows the drain's silent-probe rule, with the health pool closed last.

Socket caps are reservations: ServeHTTP claims a connection slot by compare-and-swap and a room slot in roomSlots (one slot per room however many sockets share it) before the load; the load takes over the reserved room slot, the unload or the socket's end frees it, and authorize no longer checks a cap, so the cap answers 503 before the upgrade and never 401.

Head-tracker trust needs a recent delivery: headTrustWindow 3 s since the LISTEN connection last delivered anything, computed at each call; the evictor pings dispatch_doc_ping from the shared pool after each quiet second (headPingAfter), bounded at 1 s, so a saturated pool lets trust lapse and reads fall back to the store.

The ping is gated on Service.holdsWhatTheTrackerProtects (resident rooms, read-cache entries, tracker entries, a preload) and fires after headPingAfter plus a jitter in [0, headPingAfter) redrawn on every delivery and ping, so the first holder to fire resets the rest; the gap between pings while anyone holds something stays under 2 s plus a delivery, inside the 3 s trust window.

Tracker entries carry a holds count (roomLoaded/roomUnloaded, documentReads.put/remove, offerPreload/takePreload/withdraw, coldRead around its token); an entry goes once it has no holds, no own write in flight and no unseen write end. Dropping is safe because a token is only taken under a hold, a re-made entry draws a new generation from the process-wide counter so an old token never matches, and head() is untrusted with no entry. An own write keeps or makes its entry for its duration, so tokens taken during it are untrusted.
